sourcedFrom: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet (undated — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: The Stallion is named on the heading of Uberti's single-action book as the 1873 S.A. STALLION, and it strips the way the rest of that book's revolvers do: gate open, base pin out, cylinder out sideways. It is the scaled-down gun in the line, so the parts are smaller but the sequence is identical.

steps.title: Half cock, gate open, all six chambers looked at
steps.action: With the muzzle in a safe direction, bring the hammer back to half cock and swing the loading gate open. Half cock is what frees the cylinder to rotate toward the gate, so from here you can index each chamber past the opening and actually see it. Do all six and count them — this is a one-at-a-time gun and there is no way to see the whole cylinder at once.
steps.aside: Close the loading gate after you are sure that all six chambers in your revolver are empty.
steps.quote: Draw the hammer back to the half cock position (you can also hear this click if you listen carefully). In doing this, you actually disengage the cylinder allowing it to rotate freely in the direction of the loading gate.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — B - LOADING/UNLOADING (HALF COCK) POSITION, p.1 (single-page leaflet, no printed folio)

steps.title: Every case pushed clear with the ejector rod
steps.action: Work the ejector rod under the barrel through each chamber in turn, driving it to the end of its travel rather than nudging it. On the smaller Stallion cases a half stroke will free the case without ejecting it, and the loose case then rides round and stops the cylinder. Empty chambers get the same stroke — that is how you find the one you missed.
steps.quote: Operate the ejector rod in each chamber to its full length to assure full length  case ejection.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — UNLOADING, p.1
steps.warn: Make certain you have the exact caliber cartridges matching the exact caliber of your revolver.

steps.title: Hammer down on the safety notch, never on a live round
steps.action: Uberti is explicit that the hammer rests on an empty or spent chamber, never on a loaded one, and that the safety it provides is one you have to choose to use. Identify which safety your gun carries while you are here: a small slot at the rear of the hammer means a hammer block; no slot means the safety is built into an elongated cylinder base pin instead.
steps.aside: These guns have a hammer block safety in the hammer. If you see a small slot at the rear of the hammer, then your hammer has a safety already inserted.
steps.quote: Always let the hammer rest on an empty or spent cartridge. Never rest the hammer on a loaded cartridge. Never!!
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — Hammer positions, introduction, p.1

steps.title: Empty confirmed, gate open, hammer at its half-cock notch
steps.action: Uberti opens the cleaning strip by repeating the empty check, then sets the two conditions the cylinder needs to come out: gate open and hammer at half cock. Both matter mechanically — the gate is the exit, and half cock is what pulls the bolt down out of the cylinder's locking notches. Neither is a formality you can skip because the gun is already clear.
steps.quote: Check first to make sure your revolver is empty. Then remove the cylinder using the following steps:
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, opening line, p.1

steps.title: The plunger on the frame's left front, pressed and held
steps.action: The base pin catch is the small spring-loaded plunger on the left front of the frame, forward of the cylinder. Press it in and hold it in for the whole of the next step. It is a detent sitting in a groove on the base pin; release it early and it snaps back into the groove and stops the pin dead, usually with the pin half out.
steps.quote: Depress the base pin catch. This is the spring loaded plunger which is located on the left front side of the frame. Keep it depressed.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, step 3, p.1

steps.title: Base pin out forward, all the way
steps.action: Draw the base pin forward out of the frame while the catch is still held down. Take it right out — a pin left part way still threads the cylinder and nothing will come free. Uberti calls out that this pin is a bearing surface, not just a retainer, so how clean and how oiled it is decides how the action feels.
steps.quote: Slide the base pin all the way out. The base pin is the heavy pin around which the cylinder revolves (and provides a bearing surface for the cylinder). It should always be clean and lubricated.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, step 4, p.1

steps.title: Cylinder rolled out through the gate side
steps.action: Tip the cylinder out of the frame window on the loading-gate side and catch it — on the small-frame Stallion it will drop the moment it clears. The fit is deliberately close. If it binds, back off and check the hammer has not slipped off half cock rather than forcing it out of the window.
steps.caution: The cylinder is made to fit your revolver precisely and can be removed and replaced  easily, but carefully. It is a close fit, so don’t force it to move in any direction.
steps.quote: Remove cylinder toward the loading gate.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, step 5, p.1

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: That is the full extent of the strip in Uberti's book: cylinder off, base pin out, frame intact. Everything deeper — hand, bolt, main spring, the hammer safety bar — appears only as a numbered part in the parts list, with no procedure attached, so it is not documented here either. Clean these three pieces and reverse the sequence.
steps.quote: To reassemble, simply reverse the steps used in removal.
steps.cite: Uberti Single Action Revolver and Revolving Carbine Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code or revision is printed on the leaflet — CLEANING, reassembly note, p.1
steps.warn: NEVER use cartridges marked “High Speed” or “High Velocity”.

deepAbsentReason: The single-action leaflet documents one disassembly only — the five-step cylinder removal under CLEANING — and then stops. The parts list names the backstrap, trigger guard, main spring, sear and bolt spring, hand, hammer safety bar and firing pin, but the document attaches no procedure to any of them, and a parts list is an identification aid rather than a teardown. ⚠ ONE FURTHER SCOPE NOTE, RECORDED NOT APPLIED: the leaflet carries a SPECIAL WARNING FOR CAL. 22 about seating rimfire cartridges fully so the rim does not catch the frame or gate. This catalog row is the .38 Special Stallion, so that warning is scoped away from it by chambering; it is surfaced as a caliber-conditional aside rather than as a step, because the manual states it by caliber and not by model.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Scrub bore and chambers with a good cleaning solution on a wood, aluminium or brass rod — never a steel one
Run the brush right through before reversing; never turn it round while it is still in the bore or a chamber
Follow with clean patches through bore and every chamber until they come out clean

cleaning.name: BASE PIN, CYLINDER & FRAME
tasks: Wipe the base pin along its full length and lightly oil it before it goes back
Clear the base pin hole, the frame window and the recoil shield around the gate opening
Wipe the cylinder's ratchet and its front face where it runs against the barrel

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE & BRASS
tasks: Oil the entire revolver completely but lightly once dry
Polish the brass backstrap and trigger guard with a good brass polish
Wipe the grip down rather than wetting it

reassembly: Bring the cylinder back into the frame window from the loading-gate side with the hammer at half cock.
Feed the base pin back through the frame and cylinder and push it fully home.
Confirm the base pin catch has snapped back to its regular position instead of sitting on top of the pin.
Press the plunger and check it moves freely and returns under its own spring pressure.
Shut the loading gate and lower the hammer into its safety notch.
fncheck: Confirm the revolver is empty, then run Uberti's own published check on the base pin catch — depress the plunger and confirm it both moves freely and springs back on its own, which is what proves the base pin is captured. Open the gate, set half cock and confirm the cylinder rotates freely toward the gate and locks up as the bolt drops into each notch. Confirm the hammer reaches its safety notch and full cock, and never pull the trigger at any position other than full cock.
